name: kalcutter/bitshuffle
workload: Bit-transpose (Bitshuffle) of typed data blocks, encode and decode, used as a pre-filter for compression; not a bit-width packer.
claimed_speedup: typical speedup between 1.3x and 10x depending on CPU architecture, function, and arguments
tradeoffs: Only the core transpose is provided (no HDF5/Python filter, no compression). Little-endian only. Runtime CPU dispatch needs GNU IFUNC. Block size must be a multiple of 8 elements. Header is usable from C and C++.
caveats: README gives a single range with no per-CPU table, no compiler flags, no CPU model and no benchmark code link, so first-party partial methodology. Adjacent to rather than inside integer bit-packing (bit transposition of typed arrays); category fit may be wrong. Baseline is another bitshuffle implementation, not varint, Simple8b or FastPFor. License taken from the repo page summary; the LICENSE path I tried on raw.githubusercontent.com returned 404, so confirm the exact license files.
found_via: GitHub: WebSearch 'bitshuffle OR bit unpacking AVX-512 vpmultishiftqb integers pack unpack C++ Parquet RLE bit-packed decoder faster' surfaced the repo page

name: Apache Arrow Parquet AVX-512 bit-unpacking patch (PR 14674, not merged)
baseline: Apache Arrow's existing Parquet bit-unpacking path (pre-patch scalar/SIMD code in the Parquet decoder)
workload: Parquet dictionary-index decoding (BM_DictDecodingInt64_literals in parquet-encoding-benchmark) using bit-unpack with Icelake-class AVX-512 instructions, bit widths up to 16 initially.
claimed_speedup: up to 55% performance improvement observed on Intel ICX platform
hardware: Intel ICX (Icelake-class) platform; exact CPU model not given
stars_or_usage: 17.2k stars (apache/arrow); the patch itself is a closed PR
tradeoffs: Hand-written AVX-512 intrinsics for Icelake and newer only; initial version covered bit widths of 16 or fewer, with 17 to 32 planned. Reviewers raised maintainability, MSVC and Boost-dependency concerns.
caveats: The PR was closed on 2023-03-30 for inactivity and never merged, so the code lives only in the PR diff, not in the library. Single headline number with no table, CPU model or compiler flags. The related issue 14672 gives no numbers. The incumbent is Arrow's own unpacker, not varint, Simple8b or FastPFor. Weak entry; flag for retier or rejection as off-baseline. Related Velox discussions 2353 and 4918 are about a repo already in the catalog.
